questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The research team is conducting experiments on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease.

options.text: Experiments have been conducted on a new drug that could have revolutionised the treatment of the disease through the research team.
Experiments were being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.
Experiments are conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease from the research team.
Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The research team is conducting experiments on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "experiments on a new drug" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "is conducting" to "are being conducted" (present continuous passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the research team."
 
• Ensure the additional information "that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Experiments have been conducted on a new drug that could have revolutionised the treatment of the disease through the research team." – Incorrect tense (present perfect).
 
• **Option 2: **"Experiments were being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team." – Incorrect tense (past continuous).
 
• **Option 3: **"Experiments are conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease from the research team." – Incorrect preposition (from instead of by) and tense (present simple).

__
 
• In English, the **passive voice is formed by **using the verb 'to be' + past participle (V3) of the main verb.
 
• The **past participle** of 'invite' is **'invited'.**
 
• The **original sentence** is in the** simple past** tense, and hence the passive form should also be in the simple past tense.

• **"We are invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding."** This sentence is in the present simple tense, not the simple past tense.
 
• **"We had been invited to Daniel and Mary’s wedding**." This sentence is in the past perfect tense, not the simple past tense.
